question_text: Find the product of the lengths of the perpendiculars from any point on the hyperbola x²/16 − y²/9 = 1 to its asymptotes.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State the formula
steps.margin_note: First mark. The asymptotes, in bx±ay=0 form, feed a ready-made product formula.
steps.memory_tip: The product of perpendiculars to the asymptotes of any hyperbola is always a²b²/(a²+b²).

lines.text: b²x₁² − a²y₁² = a²b² since (x₁, y₁) is on

steps.why: The two asymptotes, written with a common denominator, become the pair of lines bx∓ay=0; the standard result for the product of perpendicular distances from any point on the curve to this pair simplifies to a²b²/(a²+b²) using the hyperbola equation itself.
common_mistakes: Writing the asymptotes as ax±by=0 instead of bx±ay=0.
Writing the product formula with a minus sign, a²b²/(a²−b²), instead of a²b²/(a²+b²).

steps.label: Evaluate
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Substitute a² and b² directly into the formula.

steps.why: Substituting the values of a² and b² read off the standard form gives the numeric product directly.
common_mistakes: Adding a² and b² incorrectly, or dividing by the wrong sum.
Leaving the answer as an unsimplified fraction when 144/25 is already in lowest terms and should stay as a fraction.
